objectives: Establish the identity of a person in the way that the Civil Procedure Code requires, including without an identity document.
Decide who signs for a minor, a person under judicial disability and a company.
Handle participants who cannot read, see, hear or speak, or who do not know Bulgarian.
Check a power of attorney before the office relies on it.
Read the current status of a company in the Commercial Register.

cards.front: What three things does the notary check about each participant before a deed?
cards.back: **Identity, capacity to act and representative power** ([[gpk:578:4]]).

cards.front: How is identity established without an identity document?
cards.back: With **two witnesses** whose identity is established ([[gpk:578:5]]).
Identity card; passport (incl. diplomatic, service, seaman's); military ID card; **driving licence** ([[zbld:13:1]]).

cards.front: Who may access the National Population Database individually?
cards.back: Only **notaries and assistant notaries** in the register ([[nnbd:2:1|Art. 2(1)]] of the access ordinance).

cards.front: What can the population database show besides the address?
cards.back: Legal restrictions, marital status, marriage and divorce, death data, relatives ([[nnbd:3:2|Art. 3(2)]] of the access ordinance).

cards.front: Parents want to mortgage their child's flat for their own loan. Is that possible?
cards.back: Only by **exception**: the court may permit a pledge or a mortgage for a clear benefit of the child or an extraordinary need of the family ([[sk:130:4]]). A gift, a waiver or a loan by the minor is void.

cards.front: Who signs for a person under full judicial disability?
cards.back: The **guardian**, with court permission for dispositions ([[zls:5]]; [[sk:165:4]]).

cards.front: How does an illiterate person sign a notarial deed?
cards.back: With the print of the **right thumb**; a notarial deed is **not** countersigned by witnesses ([[gpk:579:2|Art. 579(2)]] and [[gpk:189|189 ГПК]]).

cards.front: A buyer speaks only Greek, and the notary knows no Greek. What follows?
cards.back: The notary appoints an **interpreter** ([[gpk:582]]), who promises to translate truly and signs ([[gpk:585]]).

cards.front: The seller has no document and brings his brother and a clerk of the office as witnesses. What follows?
cards.back: Neither may witness: a relative of a party ([[gpk:584::3|Art. 584 item 3]] with [[gpk:575]]) and an employee of the office ([[gpk:584::6|Art. 584 item 6]]) are excluded.

cards.front: Which law governs the capacity of a foreigner?
cards.back: The law of the state of **citizenship** ([[kmchp:50:1]]).

cards.front: A procurator signs a deed to sell the company's warehouse. What does the office check?
cards.back: A **special authorisation** for real estate ([[tz:22:2]]); the procuration alone does not cover a sale or an encumbrance of real estate.

cards.front: Who decides on the disposal of real estate in an OOD?
What form does a power of attorney for a sale of real estate need?
cards.back: Written, with **signature and content certified at the same time** ([[zzd:37]]).

quiz.question: A seller lost the identity card yesterday and has no other document. Can the deed proceed?
options: Yes, with two witnesses whose identity is established
No; the act is postponed until a new card is issued
Yes, if the seller shows a photo of the card on a phone
Yes, if the buyer confirms the identity of the seller
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:578:5]]: a person without an identity document proves identity with two witnesses whose identity is established and who meet [[gpk:584|Art. 584]] (no relatives, beneficiaries or office staff). Postponing is a common office habit, not the law; a photo or the buyer's word proves nothing.

quiz.question: Who may perform the check in the National Register of Bulgarian Identity Documents?
options: The notary or the assistant notary
Any employee of the office
The client, from a public portal
The clerk, with the notary's password
quiz.explanation: [[nnrbld:2|Art. 2]] of the ordinance on the register of identity documents: only notaries and assistant notaries have individual access; the access is personal and audited ([[nnbd:10|Art. 10]]–[[nnbd:11|11]] of the population-database ordinance). A clerk with the notary's password breaks the rule.

quiz.question: A 16-year-old wants to sell an inherited plot. What is needed?
options: The minor signs with a parent's consent, and the district court permits
The minor signs alone; an inherited plot is personal property
A parent signs alone in the name of the minor, as legal representative
Nothing is possible until the minor turns 18 and signs alone
quiz.explanation: [[zls:4]]: a minor from 14 to 18 acts personally with the consent of a parent; [[sk:130:3]] adds the permission of the district court for a disposal of real estate. A parent signs alone only for a child under 14 ([[zls:3]]).

quiz.question: Parents want to donate an apartment of their 10-year-old child to the grandmother. What is the position?
options: The gift is void; a minor cannot make a gift
It is valid with the permission of the court
It is valid if both parents sign the deed
It is valid if the grandmother accepts it
quiz.explanation: [[sk:130:4]]: a gift, a waiver of rights, a loan and a security for another's debt by a minor are void; the court may allow only a pledge or a mortgage, as an exception. Signatures and acceptance cannot cure a void act.

quiz.question: An elderly seller cannot explain what the deed does, and a nephew keeps answering. What should happen?
options: The notary talks with the seller alone; if the will is unclear, the act waits
The nephew signs for the seller as the person who answered the questions
The act proceeds, because the seller holds a valid identity card
The clerk decides whether the seller understands the deed and its effects
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:20]]: the notary meets the person alone; [[znnd:25:1|Art. 25(1)]] requires the notary to clarify the will. A contract by a person who cannot understand or control the acts is voidable ([[zzd:31]]). A valid identity card proves identity, not capacity; nobody signs for the seller without a power.

quiz.question: Which person can be a witness for identity before the notary?
options: An unrelated adult neighbour who gains nothing from the deed
The brother of the buyer, with a valid identity card
A clerk of the notary office who knows the seller for years
A clerk of the registry office who will enter the deed
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:584]] excludes persons without capacity, persons illiterate in Bulgarian, relatives of the parties or of the notary in the degrees of [[gpk:575|Art. 575]], beneficiaries of the act, blind, deaf and mute persons, and the staff of the notary office and of the registry office.

quiz.question: A deaf and illiterate person is a seller. What does the notary do?
options: Appoints a sign language interpreter and notes it
Refuses the act until a guardian is appointed
Asks the person to read the deed and nod agreement
Lets a relative sign the deed in the person's name
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:583]] has two cases: a literate deaf or mute person reads the deed and states agreement, a mute person in writing (paragraph 1); an illiterate deaf, mute or deaf-mute person needs a Bulgarian sign language interpreter appointed by the notary and noted in the act (paragraphs 2–3). That interpreter may be a relative ([[gpk:584::3|Art. 584 item 3]]).

quiz.question: A German citizen aged 18 wants to sign in Bulgaria. Which law decides the capacity?
options: German law, as the law of citizenship
Bulgarian law, because the act is in Bulgaria
The law of the state where the German lives
The law that the notary finds more suitable
quiz.explanation: [[kmchp:50:1]]: the capacity of a natural person follows the law of the state of citizenship. A Bulgarian who is also a citizen of another state counts as Bulgarian ([[kmchp:48:2|Art. 48(2)]]).

quiz.question: The manager of an OOD wants to sell the company's office. What does the office ask for?
options: The current status in the register and the decision of the general meeting
Only the identity card of the manager and the deed of the office
The tax returns of the company for the last three years and its balance sheet
The written consent of the employees who work in the office that is sold
quiz.explanation: The manager represents the company ([[tz:141:2]]), which the office checks in the Commercial Register ([[ztr:10]]); the disposal of real estate needs a decision of the general meeting ([[tz:137:1:7|Art. 137(1) item 7]]), in the form of [[tz:137:4|Art. 137(4)]].

quiz.question: A power of attorney says "to manage my apartment and collect the rent". Can the agent sell the apartment with it?
options: No; the scope does not cover a sale
Yes; management includes a sale at a fair price
Yes; the notary may widen the scope at the signing
Yes, with the consent of the buyer and the bank
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:39]]: the scope of the power is what the principal stated; "to manage" and "to collect the rent" do not include a sale. Nobody widens a power except the principal, in the form of [[zzd:37|Art. 37]].

quiz.question: The principal died a week ago. The agent wants to sign a sale under the power of attorney. What is the rule?
options: The power ended with the death of the principal
The power stays valid for one more month after the death
The power stays valid, because a notary certified it
The power stays valid until the heirs revoke it
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:41]]: a power of attorney ends with the death or the judicial disability of the principal or the agent; a certification does not prolong it, and the heirs need not revoke it. An agent who signs after the death acts without power ([[zzd:42|Art. 42]]).

quiz.question: How does a literate blind person sign a private document?
options: Signs, and two witnesses countersign the document
Puts a thumbprint, and nobody countersigns
Signs through an interpreter appointed by the notary
Signs, and the notary countersigns for the person
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:189:2]]: a private document of a literate blind person is countersigned by two witnesses. The thumbprint is for a person who cannot sign at all ([[gpk:189:1|Art. 189(1)]]); a notarial deed is never countersigned by witnesses ([[gpk:579:2|Art. 579(2)]]).
